result.title: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Project page: https://jhxcho.github.io/voda/
result.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables object-level operations on Gaussian primitives, yet existing segmentation methods are largely trained and evaluated through rendered views. This mismatch can produce accurate rendered masks from incomplete 3D selections since alpha-blended feature supervision concentrates learning on dominant contributors while leaving occluded or low-contribution Gaussians weakly supervised. We propose VODA, a plug-and-play supervision objective that exploits local depth structure to group per-pixel contributors and directly supervises all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, bypassing contribution-weighted gradient delivery. To evaluate volumetric completeness, we introduce Removal-3D, a synthetic object-removal benchmark, and the Removal Depth Error (RDE), a metric comparing predicted and ground-truth depth changes. Across four rendering-based baselines, VODA consistently improves volumetric segmentation on Removal-3D while maintaining or improving performance on LERF and ScanNet. Further analysis shows that VODA recovers lower-contribution Gaussians, while simple gradient reweighting and spatial propagation fail to reproduce comparable gains.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 VODA：利用局部深度结构对逐像素的贡献者分组，直接监督所选深度簇内的全部高斯，以缓解 alpha 混合渲染监督只学主导贡献者、遮挡或弱贡献高斯监督不足的问题；同时构建 Removal-3D 基准与 Removal Depth Error 指标来评估三维分割的体素完备性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「渲染掩码正确但三维选择不完整」的失配、以及按混合权重分配监督导致弱贡献元素被忽略的分析，可能为 LVR 中 latent 是否真正承载视觉证据、贡献分配与视觉证据筛选的评价提供类比线索；分组监督与反事实移除式指标的迁移性可供核查。
